questions.text: duration ranks the training rows with an out-of-fold AUC of 0.81 on its own, far above the other features (median 0.56). Is its value really known at the prediction moment, or is it recorded at or after the outcome? (availability decided: not_available)

values.question: Does any single feature, on its own, predict the outcome so well that its availability at the prediction moment should be questioned?
values.note: Each feature alone, scored out of fold on the training rows. A high value only raises a question about when the value is known; it never keeps or drops a feature, and a legitimate feature may score high.

warnings: job = unknown (special value): only 26 training rows; its rate is too noisy to read on its own.
values.note: Rates by group on training rows are associations, not effects of the variable.
values.question: Does the positive rate differ across the groups of job by more than chance alone draws?

chart.statistic: spread between the largest and the smallest group value among groups of at least 30 training rows

null_band.note: The band is the range of the same figure after shuffling the target among the training rows 19 times (fixed seed): what chance alone draws. A pattern inside it is not distinguishable from chance; one above every shuffle happens by chance about once in 20 looks.

values.note: Counts of training rows only. A distribution describes this sample; it is not a rate of the outcome and says nothing about causes.
